Yes. NovaLearn should fund the Advanced OCR Pipeline before accelerating the Teams integration.

- **Current support demand:** Scanned PDF handling is the biggest support burden. In May 2026, 27% of support tickets were related to import issues and broken citations from scanned PDFs [NL-015-S06]. Scanned policy documents are also the primary driver of citation errors and onboarding delays [NL-001-S08]. While Teams is a highly requested feature [NL-011-S07], the current support pressure is concentrated on OCR and ingestion quality, not on Teams.

- **Onboarding impact:** Scanned PDF ingestion and OCR remain the primary onboarding bottleneck [NL-016-S01], and scanned legacy documentation is the primary technical driver of onboarding delays [NL-014-S01]. The Advanced OCR Pipeline is explicitly intended to resolve these issues and reduce onboarding friction [NL-001-S08][NL-016-S07]. Accelerating Teams without fixing OCR would risk delivering inaccurate, un-cited answers to a larger audience inside chat [NL-015-S06].

- **Roadmap status:** The Advanced OCR Pipeline is scheduled for August 2026 and is designated the highest technical priority [NL-001-S08][NL-014-S01]. Teams, by contrast, is in the design phase for Q4 2026 [NL-001-S08][NL-011-S07], with development slated for early 2027 [NL-015-S06]. Internal evidence shows the Teams connector is still in an early proof-of-concept phase, lacking security controls and tenant isolation, and is not ready for customer deployment [NL-023-S04]. Rushing it would risk a tenant-isolation breach and require a complete auth-layer redesign [NL-015-S06].

Thus, the evidence supports keeping OCR first: it addresses the current support demand, removes the primary onboarding bottleneck, and follows the official roadmap, while Teams remains an early-stage, security-sensitive effort.
